blocks.heading: Choosing between locations
blocks.text: A supported location choice identifies the business’s needs, compares the relevant alternatives and gives weight to the decisive constraint. Use the stated customer, input, labour, reliability and cost facts. A location can suit one enterprise and not another; low wages do not establish low unit labour cost without productivity evidence. Recognise uncertainty and the condition that would change the choice. Do not invent sales, subsidies or infrastructure just to justify a preferred place.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Oru Repairs serves urgent local customers. Its current town has suitable skills and short response times. An alternative foreign site offers lower rent but makes urgent visits impossible; no remote service substitute is available. Remain near the customers because response access is essential to this service and the rent saving does not replace it. A standard non-urgent product with dependable delivery could justify another balance.
